title: Fabrication & Release Review
description: Checks that the fabrication package, drawing, stackup, panel and release records are complete and match the fabricator's capability before the board is ordered.

items.text: All required layers are exported: copper (top, bottom, inner), silkscreen, solder mask and paste
items.hint: Compare the layer list against the stackup; a missing inner layer is easy to miss in a zip.

items.text: The board outline (Edge.Cuts / mechanical layer) is exported correctly
items.hint: Include internal cutouts and slots, and make the outline a closed contour.

items.text: The drill file (Excellon / NC drill) is exported with correct units and zero suppression
items.hint: Overlay the drill file on copper in a CAM viewer; a units or format mismatch shows up as offset or scaled holes.

items.text: Gerber files are opened in a CAM viewer and visually checked before submission
items.hint: Use an independent viewer, not the CAD tool that made them.

items.text: File names follow the fabricator's requirements (no spaces, correct extensions)
The revision identifier is included in the file names or fab notes
items.hint: Every file and the zip itself should carry the revision so mixed-revision packages are obvious.

items.text: Gerber X2, ODB++ or IPC-2581 is used, as agreed with the fabricator
items.hint: Intelligent formats carry layer function and stackup, reducing interpretation errors.

items.text: Plated and non-plated holes are in separate drill files or clearly attributed
items.hint: Mixing them leads to plated mounting holes or unplated vias.

items.text: An IPC-D-356 netlist is included for the fabricator's electrical test
items.hint: Without it the fab tests against a netlist extracted from the Gerbers, which won't catch design-to-Gerber errors.

items.text: A drill drawing or drill table lists every hole size, symbol, quantity and plating
items.hint: Check the totals against the drill file.

items.text: A readme lists every file in the package and its function
items.hint: Include layer order, contact name and the revision.

items.text: The copper layer order is unambiguous and matches the stackup
items.hint: Name files by layer number (L1…Ln) or use X2 attributes, so inner layers can't be swapped.

items.text: The fabrication drawing is included as a PDF in the package
Each blind, buried or backdrill span has its own drill file
items.hint: Name the start and end layer of each span.

items.text: Controlled impedance requirements are specified with reference to the stackup
items.hint: Point to the impedance table rather than repeating values in several places.

items.text: Surface finish is specified (ENIG, HASL, OSP, etc.) and matches design requirements
Copper weight is specified per layer (e.g. 1 oz outer, 0.5 oz inner)
items.hint: State whether outer weights are base or finished after plating.

items.text: Solder mask and silkscreen colors are specified
Via fill / tenting requirements are specified (tented, plugged, filled)
items.hint: Name the via type and treatment, ideally using IPC-4761 types, and which vias it applies to.

items.text: The IPC-6012 performance class (Class 2 or Class 3) is specified on the fab drawing
items.hint: Class 3 costs more and limits fab choice; specify it only where needed.

items.text: The base material is specified by type and key properties, or by IPC-4101 slash sheet
items.hint: "FR-4" alone covers a wide range of materials; name Tg and, if needed, Td and Dk.

items.text: Material Tg and Td suit lead-free assembly and the operating temperature
items.hint: Mid- or high-Tg material is typical for lead-free, thick or high-layer-count boards; confirm per fab capability.

items.text: Finished board thickness and tolerance are specified
items.hint: Say where it is measured (over copper, over mask); it matters for edge connectors and card guides.

items.text: Finished hole size tolerances are specified for plated and non-plated holes
items.hint: Tolerances tighter than standard (press-fit, locating pins) must be called out explicitly.

items.text: Flammability rating is specified where the product needs it (e.g. UL 94 V-0)
items.hint: Check the safety standard for the product; the fab must use a recognized material and process.

items.text: Plated edges and castellated holes are called out on the drawing
items.hint: Both need special process steps; the fab will not add them unprompted.

items.text: Edge connector bevel angle and depth are specified
items.hint: Card-edge fingers need a bevel to mate cleanly; follow the connector spec.

items.text: The fab drawing has a stackup with layer order, copper weights, dielectric thicknesses and materials
The stackup is confirmed by the fabricator with their actual materials before release
items.hint: A stackup built from catalog values can't always be made. Get the fab's stackup back in writing.

items.text: The stackup is symmetric about its center
items.hint: Asymmetric copper or dielectric causes bow and twist after lamination and reflow.

items.text: The impedance table lists each target, tolerance, layer, reference planes and trace geometry
items.hint: Include differential pairs with both width and spacing.

items.text: Dk and loss tangent used in design are at the relevant frequency and confirmed by the fab
items.hint: Datasheet Dk is often quoted at a lower frequency than the signal of interest.

items.text: Dielectric thicknesses in the CAD stackup match the fab-confirmed stackup
items.hint: Re-run impedance calculations if the fab changed any thickness or material.

items.text: The fab may adjust trace widths to hit impedance, within stated limits
items.hint: State the maximum adjustment allowed so the fab can tune without breaking spacing rules.

items.text: Heavy-copper layers meet the fab's minimum spacing and resin-fill capability
items.hint: Heavy copper needs wider spacing and thicker prepreg to fill between features.

items.text: Dielectric thickness between isolated layers meets the insulation requirement
items.hint: Check against the safety standard's requirement for insulation through the board.

items.text: The smallest plated drill and board thickness are within the fab's aspect-ratio capability
items.hint: Rule of thumb: through-hole aspect ratio around 8:1 to 10:1 for standard processes; confirm with the fab.

items.text: Annular rings meet the fab's capability for the specified IPC class
Hole wall plating thickness is specified, or set by the IPC-6012 class
items.hint: Thicker plating improves via reliability under thermal cycling.

items.text: Microvia aspect ratio and size are within the fab's capability
items.hint: Rule of thumb: microvia depth no more than about its diameter; confirm with the fab.

items.text: Stacked versus staggered microvias are agreed with the fab
items.hint: Stacked microvias need filled vias and cost more; some fabs advise staggering for reliability.

items.text: Via-in-pad vias are filled and plated over (capped)
items.hint: Usually IPC-4761 Type VII. Unfilled via-in-pad wicks solder away from BGA and QFN joints.

items.text: Backdrill depth, maximum stub length and must-not-cut layers are specified
items.hint: Give it per net or per drill span, matched to the backdrill file.

items.text: Slots and non-round holes are defined in the drill or rout file and on the drawing
items.hint: Plated slots in particular are often lost or made as round holes.

items.text: Press-fit holes are listed in the drill table with their finished size and tolerance
items.hint: Use the connector manufacturer's hole specification; plating thickness affects the finished size.

items.text: Solder mask expansion around pads meets the fab's registration capability
Solder mask web between fine-pitch pads meets the fab's minimum
items.hint: Below the minimum, the fab will remove the web silently. Decide whether that is acceptable.

items.text: Mask openings exist for test points, fiducials and intentionally exposed copper
There is no unintended exposed copper near pads or traces
items.hint: Look for mask openings on vias or traces that could short to parts or chassis.

items.text: Silkscreen is clipped clear of pads and exposed copper
Silkscreen text height and line width meet the fab's minimum
items.hint: Rule of thumb: around 0.15 mm (6 mil) line width and 0.8–1.0 mm (31–39 mil) text height for legibility.

items.text: Safety markings (high-voltage warnings, isolation boundaries) are on the silkscreen
items.hint: Check the product's safety standard for required symbols.

items.text: The surface finish suits the finest-pitch parts and their flatness needs
items.hint: HASL is uneven and generally a poor fit for fine pitch and BGA; ENIG, OSP or immersion finishes are flatter.

items.text: The finish suits any wire bonding, press-fit or contact areas
items.hint: Check connector and bonding requirements; ENEPIG or hard gold may be needed.

items.text: The finish's shelf life suits the build schedule
items.hint: OSP and immersion silver or tin degrade with storage time; plan build dates accordingly.

items.text: The finish is lead-free where RoHS compliance is required
items.hint: Specify lead-free HASL rather than plain HASL if HASL is used.

items.text: Hard gold areas (edge fingers, contact pads) have a specified thickness
items.hint: Thickness depends on mating cycles; follow the connector or contact spec.

items.text: Panel size and array configuration are agreed with the fabricator
items.hint: Also confirm them with the assembler: the panel is their unit of work.

items.text: V-score or tab-route breakaway method is specified and consistent
items.hint: V-score only works for straight edges that run the full panel width.

items.text: Rails, tooling holes and fiducials are included in the panel design
items.hint: Follow the assembler's preferred rail width and tooling hole size.

items.text: Copper balance across the panel is checked to minimize warpage
items.hint: Add copper thieving on rails and empty areas if layers are unbalanced.

items.text: Panel dimensions fit the assembler's line limits
items.hint: Check both minimum and maximum conveyor sizes and the maximum panel weight.

items.text: Components near break lines keep a safe distance and MLCCs run parallel to the break line
items.hint: Break stress cracks ceramic capacitors. Keep clearance per assembler guidance.

items.text: Parts that overhang the board edge have clearance cutouts in the panel
A panel drawing is included in the release package
items.hint: Dimension the array, rails, tooling holes, fiducials and break features.

items.text: V-score depth, angle and residual web are specified per fab capability
The depanelization method won't overstress nearby components
items.hint: Hand breaking and pizza-cutter separation flex the board; routing is gentler for sensitive parts.

items.text: The policy for scrapped boards in a panel (X-outs) is agreed
items.hint: Some assemblers reject panels containing X-outs, or charge extra for them.

items.text: 100% bare-board electrical test is required
items.hint: Flying probe for prototypes, fixture test for volume.

items.text: Electrical test uses the CAD netlist (IPC-D-356), not one extracted from the Gerbers
Impedance coupons are required with a TDR test report
items.hint: Make sure the coupon matches the actual trace geometry and reference planes.

items.text: Microsection (cross-section) reports are requested
items.hint: Show plating thickness, registration and laminate quality.

items.text: A certificate of conformance is requested with each lot
Insulation or hipot testing between isolated nets is specified for the bare board
items.hint: Define the test voltage, duration and which nets are tested.

items.text: Bare-board ionic cleanliness testing is specified
items.hint: Residues on the bare board can cause leakage and corrosion under coating.

items.text: Final DRC is run on the production-ready files with zero errors
items.hint: Re-run after the last edit, including silkscreen and fill updates.

items.text: The design is compared with the previous revision for unintended changes
items.hint: Use a Gerber or CAD diff; check that only the ECO's changes appear.

items.text: The fabricator's DFM check has passed, or all flagged issues are resolved
items.hint: Record the decision on each flagged item.

items.text: The Gerber zip includes all required files and nothing extraneous
A checksum (e.g. MD5 or SHA-256) of the final package is recorded
items.hint: Lets you prove later which exact files were ordered.

items.text: DRC rules match the chosen fabricator's capability, not tool defaults
There are no unrouted connections
items.hint: Check the ratsnest is empty, including after copper pours are refilled.

items.text: Copper-to-edge clearance meets the fab's capability for the chosen edge process
items.hint: V-score and routed edges need different clearances; inner-layer planes need pullback too.

items.text: Gerbers are compared to the CAD netlist after export
items.hint: A CAM netlist compare catches export errors such as missing pours or flashed pads.

items.text: Creepage and clearance are checked against the safety requirement
items.hint: Check on every layer, including inner layers and between pad edges.

items.text: Drill-to-copper clearance on inner layers meets fab capability
items.hint: Drill wander causes shorts to inner planes if clearance is too small.

items.text: Any DRC waivers are documented with a reason
The Gerber package is committed to version control at the correct tag or revision
The fab order confirmation number is recorded and linked to the design revision
Any deviations from the standard process are documented and approved
Design files are locked and archived at the release revision
items.hint: Include schematic, PCB, libraries and output settings, so the release can be regenerated.

items.text: The revision marked on the board (copper or silkscreen) matches the release revision
Fab, assembly, BOM and centroid outputs are all from the same release revision
items.hint: Release them together as one package to avoid mixing revisions.

items.text: An ECO or change list records what changed from the previous revision
Design review sign-offs are recorded before release
items.hint: Include schematic, layout and this fab review, with reviewer names and dates.

items.text: Open issues and errata from the previous revision are resolved or carried forward
Bend areas are defined on the drawing with bend radius and static or dynamic use
Bend radius meets the fab's minimum for the flex thickness
items.hint: Rule of thumb: about 10× thickness for static bends and much more for dynamic flexing; confirm with the fab.

items.text: No vias or pads are placed in bend areas
Traces in bend areas run perpendicular to the bend line and are staggered between layers
items.hint: Stacked traces on adjacent layers raise strain and crack sooner.

items.text: Coverlay openings meet fab capability, and coverlay versus flexible mask is chosen
Stiffeners are specified with material, thickness, location and adhesive
Rigid-to-flex transition zones keep vias and pads at a safe distance
items.hint: Distance per fab capability; components close to the transition stress the flex.

items.text: Rolled-annealed copper is specified for dynamic flex areas
items.hint: Electrodeposited copper cracks sooner under repeated flexing.

items.text: ZIF tail thickness, including stiffener, matches the connector specification
items.hint: Too thin and the contacts don't grip; too thick and the tail won't insert.
